title: Render load ramp, member stress, breakage, and replay
description: Render the selected candidate bridge on Canvas 2D as its hanging weight increases. Communicate load, member stress, each break/cascade, and final collapse; allow a completed candidate or champion to be replayed.
design: Use Canvas 2D with device-pixel-ratio-aware sizing. Keep simulation evaluation separate from animation: the solver supplies a break-event timeline and the renderer interpolates the weight between events. Support a reduced-motion mode that still exposes the same numeric state.
acceptance_criteria: The load visibly rises through solver break events; members are visually differentiated by tension/compression/stress state; failed members visibly separate or disappear; the final stable load and failure state are shown; replay uses recorded deterministic failure events and does not mutate the candidate.

title: Add structural solver and failure regression tests
description: Add automated tests for equilibrium, supports, force signs, capacity limits, cascades, instability, and deterministic results so the simulation can evolve without silently changing its meaning.
design: Keep the mechanics tests independent of browser rendering. Prefer the platform test runner or a small dependency-free harness that fits the chosen static-module setup.
acceptance_criteria: Tests cover at least a simply supported test truss with a known reaction, a tension failure, a compression/buckling failure, a post-break redistribution/cascade, an unstable bridge, and repeatable seeded evaluation; tests run from a documented command.

title: Implement the seeded genetic algorithm engine
description: Evolve decoded bridge genomes using deterministic randomness, fitness from the agreed mechanics contract, elitism, parent selection, crossover, and mutation. Keep generation transitions independent of UI state.
design: Use an explicit seeded PRNG rather than Math.random. Start with tournament selection, one or two elites, and per-gene mutation; choose conservative defaults (e.g. population 24) but keep them configurable. Keep the GA pure and deterministic.
acceptance_criteria: A seed reproduces the same initial population and subsequent generations; selection ranks by maximum stable load with the agreed tie-break; elites survive unchanged; crossover and mutation produce valid budget-bounded genomes; population size remains fixed; unit tests demonstrate fitness does not depend on render timing.

title: Define bridge lattice, genome encoding, and viable seeds
description: Represent legal one-stick members and candidate bridge structures on the fixed-span lattice. Define deterministic genome decode/encode and a first-generation strategy that includes valid load-bearing structures as well as diverse variants.
design: Keep the genome representation independent from Canvas and the solver. Favor a compact bitset/edge-vector over all legal unit-stick edges, with bounded heights and explicit support/deck constraints. Include known truss patterns in the seed population so early generations can demonstrate meaningful results rather than all scoring zero.
acceptance_criteria: Genome decoding is deterministic for a seed; members map to legal lattice edges and never exceed the shared stick budget; endpoint supports and center load node are represented explicitly; invalid/disconnected/mechanism structures are detectable; initial candidates include viable bridges and varied topologies.

title: Implement deterministic truss solve and progressive failure
description: Implement a pure, deterministic structural evaluator for a candidate bridge under an increasing center load. Solve nodal equilibrium/member axial force, identify tension or compression-buckling failure, remove failed sticks, and redistribute load until the bridge is stable or collapses.
design: Use a small 2D linear-elastic truss stiffness solver. Make the load ramp event-driven: calculate the next load at which a capacity is reached, break/re-solve, and expose those events for smooth visual animation. This preserves the steady rising-weight experience without recomputing a dense solve for every animation frame. Treat glue joints as idealized pins in v1.
acceptance_criteria: Known small trusses produce expected reactions and member-force signs; unstable/singular structures fail safely; both tension and compression limits are enforced; broken members are removed and load is re-solved/cascaded; repeated evaluation of the same bridge and parameters returns the same failure load and break sequence.

title: Agree on v1 bridge mechanics and fitness contract
description: Review and lock the simulation assumptions before implementing the mechanics or scoring. The epic records the proposed contract: deterministic static truss mechanics, toothpick-lattice members, fixed support/load conditions, progressive failure, and capacity-based fitness. Record changes here if the intended game should instead use a different level of physical realism or construction freedom.
design: Recommended defaults: each edge is one equal-length toothpick; all joints are ideal pins with no glue failure; supports are left pin/right roller; the weight hangs from the center deck node; linear static truss analysis uses Earth gravity and displays kg-equivalent load; members fail in tension or compression/buckling; after a member breaks, solve again and cascade until stable or globally unstable. The score is the maximum stable load with a shared per-bridge stick budget. This is a toy model and must not be presented as a real build/safety calculator.
acceptance_criteria: The bridge geometry, supports, load position/units, stick budget, member and joint failure assumptions, failure/cascade rule, fitness/tie-break rule, and educational disclaimer are written down and accepted. Implementation beads can then proceed without changing the evaluation contract midstream.

title: Build an interactive genetic toothpick bridge lab
description: Create a client-side web experience inspired by the interaction loop of red42/HTML5_Genetic_Cars: visualize candidate designs, test them, evolve a population, and inspect best results. The primary simulation is a toothpick truss bridge with a hanging center load that increases until structural failure. Keep the mechanics deterministic and educational rather than claiming engineering-grade accuracy.
design: Proposed v1: static client-only app using native JavaScript modules, HTML/CSS, and Canvas 2D; no runtime framework or remote physics dependency. Use a fixed-span 2D pin-jointed truss on a one-toothpick lattice, idealized glue joints, pinned left support and roller right support, and a centered hanging load. Each candidate receives the same finite stick budget. The model computes static axial forces, tension and compression/buckling failures, removes failed members, and redistributes load until unstable. Fitness is maximum stable load (displayed as kg-equivalent at Earth gravity); use stick count as a tie-breaker. A deterministic seeded GA evolves candidates. The UI animates each candidate being loaded, highlights member stress/failure, and provides population, generation trend, replay, speed, pause/step, seed, and local save/restore. Explicitly label the simulator as an educational approximation, not real structural engineering advice. Defaults such as span, stick budget, and capacities remain configurable after the mechanics decision.
acceptance_criteria: A visitor can watch a seeded population of bridges undergo load-to-failure tests, see how each generation improves, inspect/replay the strongest bridge, and control or restart an evolution run. The model limitations are visible in the product documentation.

title: Verify accessibility, responsive behavior, and runtime performance
description: Run integrated smoke checks and refine the experience across desktop and small-screen sizes, keyboard navigation, and reduced motion. Ensure evaluating a generation does not freeze the page.
design: If generation evaluation exceeds a responsive frame budget, move pure GA/solver evaluation to a Web Worker while keeping deterministic input/output and the same test coverage.
acceptance_criteria: Core controls are labeled and keyboard reachable; canvas information has an accessible textual equivalent; contrast and focus states are usable; reduced-motion behavior is respected; a full generation completes without a long main-thread stall; smoke-test steps are recorded.

title: Document usage, model limits, and project commands
description: Explain how to run the static site, how the genetic loop and bridge scoring work, and where the approximation differs from real toothpick construction.
design: Inspect source inspiration at https://github.com/red42/HTML5_Genetic_Cars; borrow interaction concepts (seeded runs, controls, replay, score history), not code/assets unless licensing and attribution are deliberately handled.
acceptance_criteria: README explains local serving, controls, seed/reproducibility, tests, fitness, supports/load/member assumptions, and explicitly warns that the app is educational and not a structural safety calculator; any borrowed ideas/assets are attributed and license-compatible.

title: Show population gallery, rankings, and generation trends
description: Present candidate bridges and their test outcomes in a compact population view, alongside best/average performance over generations and a selectable leaderboard.
design: Keep a clear route between the animated single-bridge stage and the whole population: candidates can be tested sequentially in the stage while completed candidates accumulate results in the gallery. Offer a fast-forward mode for evaluation runs.
acceptance_criteria: Each current-generation candidate has an identifiable thumbnail/status and failure-load result; selecting a candidate displays it in the main stage; best and average load history are plotted with labeled axes; the current champion and generation are obvious; empty and first-generation states are handled.

title: Wire evolution controls and reproducible run settings
description: Connect the app to the simulation and GA with controls for starting/pausing, stepping, changing playback speed, fast-forwarding, choosing a seed, and starting a fresh population. Expose only useful v1 parameters without overwhelming the experience.
design: Keep a small default surface: run/pause, next/step, speed, new run/seed, mutation rate, and optional save/restore. Avoid adding unsupported physics knobs before the underlying model is validated.
acceptance_criteria: Pause/resume preserves the current load event; step advances one candidate or generation predictably; fast-forward completes evaluation without changing scores; reset with the same seed recreates the same run; settings changes have clear apply/reset behavior; controls work by keyboard.

title: Scaffold the static workshop UI and responsive layout
description: Build the no-build-step app shell for the bridge lab. Establish the visual language and responsive page regions before wiring the simulation.
design: Use warm toothpick/joint colors against a high-contrast workshop backdrop. Keep all controls as semantic HTML; reserve Canvas 2D for bridge rendering and graphs. Structure code into small native ES modules so the model remains testable independently of the DOM.
acceptance_criteria: The app opens from a local static server with no runtime framework/dependency; the layout includes a canvas stage, controls/metrics region, population area, and generation-history area; the interface remains usable on narrow screens and respects reduced-motion preferences.

title: Save and restore evolution runs locally
description: Persist a run snapshot in browser localStorage so users can return to a seed, population, settings, and champion without a backend.
design: Persist plain serializable state only (seed, GA settings, genomes, generation history, selected champion); do not serialize Canvas or live solver objects. Provide a clear reset/delete action.
acceptance_criteria: Users can save and restore a run; stored data is versioned and validated; invalid or obsolete data produces a recoverable message; no bridge/run data is sent to a server.
